clue.text: Drug — figure drawing it in inhaling poisonous gas?

indicators.note: drawing in means taking something inside, so the figure surrounds the next piece
completes the phrase drawing in, the figure taking the next piece inside it

parts.note: nine is a figure, a number

indicators.note: inhaling means breathing something in, so the gas goes inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written
CO is the chemical formula for carbon monoxide, a poisonous gas

explanation.surface: A question about whether a drawn figure takes in poison gas while a drug is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: IT inhaling CO gives ICOT, and 'drawing ... in' puts that inside NINE, between N and INE.
explanation.definitionFit: The addictive alkaloid in tobacco is a stimulant drug.

clue.text: A pleasing thing for Turkish generals

parts.note: a gas is informal British for something great fun

explanation.surface: Something pleasant offered to the military leaders of Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A gas' is informal for a lot of fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic Ottoman military commanders and officials held the title aga, here plural.

clue.text: Difficult as a hitch?

definitions.meaning: a hard problem is tricky and complicated
a hitch is a kind of tie in rope, so it is full of loops and ties

explanation.walkthrough: A hitch is both a problem and a kind of knot in rope, so the second reading is playful.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangled, tricky problem is described with this word, and literally it means full of tied loops.

clue.text: Where China Sea becomes choppy in the wind

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for wind

parts.note: fart is a crude word for breaking wind

indicators.note: choppy water is rough and broken, so the letters of sea are churned up

explanation.surface: The China Sea turns rough when the wind gets up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China Sea' reads as one place name, but China is the definition and Sea the anagram fodder (EAS) going inside FART.
explanation.definitionFit: China lies in the region of East Asia that Europeans call the Orient, so the clue asks where China is.

clue.text: Anticipating a comic, it having popular features inside

indicators.note: features inside means one thing contains the other, the comic holding the next pieces

parts.note: a wag is a joker, a comic person
taken as written
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: Waiting for a comedian whose act contains popular material.
explanation.definitionFit: Waiting for something means expecting or anticipating it to come.

clue.text: Settle on leading celebrities for theatre

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to foot a bill is to settle it
leading lights are prominent figures, celebrities

explanation.surface: Agreeing on the star names a theatre will put on its posters.
explanation.definitionFit: The row of lamps at the stage front is a byword for the theatre itself.

clue.text: Power of pulling, for certain?

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the answer is a run of letters within the following words

explanation.surface: Asking whether some force really comes from pulling.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads like a riddle about pulling power, but the answer sits in the letters running across 'pulling, for certain'.
explanation.definitionFit: A force measured in multiples of gravity is a kind of power acting on pilots and drivers.

Work of 15: among plays, others by him not entirely ambiguous

indicators.note: ambiguous means open to several readings, so the letters can be read in another order

parts.note: to play is to toy, so plays gives toys

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter of the phrase is dropped

explanation.surface: Among Bennett's plays, the others are said to be a little ambiguous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' drops the M of 'others by him', leaving OTHERSBYHI; with TOYS that pool is rearranged into the three-word title.
explanation.definitionFit: This 2004 school drama is one of the best-known plays by the author in 15.

clue.text: Go by land, getting cold

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: to land a prize is to win it
a go is a try, an attempt

explanation.surface: Travelling overland and catching a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather typical of the coldest season is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Bowler's dream, new balls caught in the slips

indicators.note: caught in means held inside, so the shuffled letters sit within the slips

parts.note: tickets are slips of paper

indicators.note: to ball something up is to make a mess of it, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A cricket story: new balls taken as catches by fielders in the slips.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the slips are close catching fielders, but here slips are TICKETS; 'balls' scrambles NEW to ENW, which goes after the T. Taking all ten wickets in an innings is a bowler's dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking every wicket in an innings is the rare feat any cricket bowler hopes for.

clue.text: Is the bottle so courageous?

definitions.meaning: a bottle filled with whisky or gin holds spirit, so is spirit-filled

explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for courage, which makes the first reading look like the definition too.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of spirit means lively and brave, and a bottle holding spirits is jokingly so.

clue.text: One climbed clear as English author

parts.note: a ben is a Scottish mountain, something one climbs
nett profit is the amount cleared after costs

explanation.surface: A climber who cleared the summit becomes an English writer.
explanation.walkthrough: BEN is a mountain peak in Scotland, as in Ben Nevis.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Bennett is the English playwright behind the plays in this puzzle.

clue.text: Month after one thrown from vehicle, find wing in church

indicators.note: after places the month behind the vehicle piece
thrown from means removed out of the vehicle

parts.note: a train is a vehicle
I is the Roman numeral one
Sept is short for September

explanation.surface: A month after someone was flung from a car, finding a wing of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross arms of a church building are the wings across the nave.

clue.text: Einstein's old oath about butter somewhat lost

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the oath goes round the trimmed butter

parts.note: egad is an archaic exclamation or mild oath

indicators.note: somewhat lost means part of the butter goes missing, its last letter

parts.note: ghee is clarified butter used in Indian cooking

explanation.surface: Einstein's mild old curse at losing some of his butter.
explanation.walkthrough: Einstein stands for any brainy person.
explanation.definitionFit: An intellectual, a brainy academic type, can be called by Einstein's name in jest.

clue.text: See 24 across
Number of convictions proves contradictory, thief ultimately claimed

indicators.note: claimed means taken in, so the last letter goes inside

parts.note: to belie is to show something to be false

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very last letter of thief

explanation.surface: A thief's many convictions are contradicted when he finally makes a claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Several convictions are firmly held opinions or principles.

clue.text: 5 a part rewritten with religious rite for 15's work

indicators.note: rewritten means the letters are put down again in a new order

parts.note: the number five spelt out
taken as written
unction is anointing with oil, a religious rite

explanation.surface: Five parts rewritten with a religious ceremony for a writer's script.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of FIVE APART gives APRIVATEF, and UNCTION finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1984 film comedy about a pig was scripted by Bennett, the author at 15.

clue.text: Fish put in one's ear

indicators.note: heard in one's ear means said aloud, so a word that sounds alike is wanted

parts.note: to put is to place

explanation.surface: Something fishy put into one's ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatfish common in European waters, known for orange spots.

clue.text: Shine on beyond deadly sin

indicators.note: beyond means the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: lust is one of the seven deadly sins
re means on the subject of, concerning

explanation.surface: Glowing on account of a deadly sin.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam or glossy brightness is a sheen or shine.

clue.text: Juliet's heart and Lear's desire

indicators.note: heart means the middle letters of the name

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king

explanation.surface: Two Shakespeare characters: Juliet's heart and King Lear's wishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fondness or taste for something is a desire for it.

clue.text: Copy returned shortly, thrill getting hold of terribly sad work of 15

indicators.note: returned means the shortened word is read backwards
shortly means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a fake is a copy

indicators.note: getting hold of means grasping, so the thrill holds the shuffled letters

parts.note: a kick is a thrill

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters of sad are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A copied book sent back early, the thrill gripping a gloomy piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: FAK reversed gives KAF; 'terribly' turns SAD into ASD inside KICK.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1986 play about the Prague novelist's remains is one of Bennett's stage works.

clue.text: 15's work, if a mermaid breaks off to introduce yarn from Richmond?

indicators.note: breaks means smashes up, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged
to introduce means let something in, so the yarn goes inside off

parts.note: taken as written
Richmond is the capital of the US state of Virginia
wool is yarn

explanation.surface: A mermaid breaking off to bring in yarn from Richmond for a writer's work.
explanation.walkthrough: IFAMERMAID rearranges to MEIMAFRAID; OFF splits as OF ... F around VIRGINIA WOOL. The yarn is Virginian because Richmond is the state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Bennett wrote this 1978 TV play about a lecturer, so it is a work of the author at 15.

clue.text: Story taking month, not a month less a day

indicators.note: not means the letter a is left out

parts.note: May is a month

indicators.note: less means the day is subtracted from the month

parts.note: taken as the word month itself
Mon is short for Monday

explanation.surface: A story spanning a month, give or take a day.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend or fable is a traditional story.

clue.text: Guillotine out to slice through vessel, sliced into pieces

indicators.note: to slice through means cutting into the vessel, so the piece goes inside it

parts.note: a cup is a vessel for drinking

indicators.note: a guillotine cuts off the head, so out loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A guillotine slicing through a vessel and cutting it to bits.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopped into small portions describes something sliced into pieces.
